- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–3%.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast windows; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent history shows sustained upward momentum.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day spikes; smooth out forecast peaks by reducing overshoot by 5–10% relative to immediate prior value.
- Apply mean reversion bias correction: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 2–5%.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 2–4% to avoid runaway bias.
- For forecasts with high variance in early days, apply a 1–2% downward bias to avoid overconfidence in short-term volatility.
